dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: An easy-breezy Natlan in an easy-breezy summer! Welcome to the Shoal's Haven! Ah, here comes someone with an aroma of freshness...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An aroma of freshness?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Absolutely. My nose is sharp enough to tell the difference between today's catch and yesterday's catch, as well as tell fresh customers apart from overnight people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What exactly is an "overnight person"?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: They're like a fish that was caught the night before — they smell a little off. Take Teuciztli, for example...

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: He'll keep leftover seafood from the day before and continue to sell it. But just one day is enough to pollute the freshness with a little bit of decay.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Even though eating it won't make you sick, we take pride in selling fresh food every day. So, just like his fish, Teuciztli is very much "overnight".

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: But as long as I'm here, you can rest assured that I'll give you only the freshest fish. I can't stand the stench of cooking with anything less, and that's why I throw out all the old fish on the sly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not scared the boss'll find out?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: He won't find out if you don't snitch. You're fresh, people like you don't mix with his type.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: (Lawaia gives you a playful wink.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's business today?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: It's not bad at all. What's strange, though, is today's catch was suddenly much fresher.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: The boss even came to tell me that I'd been working hard lately, and he gave me some Mora as thanks. Talk about a turnaround...

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: I'm starting to suspect something... Did he hear about the things I said?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Bah, whatever. It's not every day that free Mora just falls into your lap. Here, have some — consider it a token of good fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Take care, and I hope you enjoy your stay.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: An easy-breezy Natlan in an easy-breezy summer! Welcome to The Dewdrop bar... Oh hey, it's you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Hah! I was brought here by the whims of fate!

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Just a few days after we met, all of a sudden, Teuciztli said I had to go. I wonder if someone was speaking ill about me...

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Don't make that face. It was just a job — it's no big loss.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: And when I got here, I realized it was actually a good thing. Don't you agree the scenery on Tete Isle is much better than Easybreeze Market?

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: There aren't so many fresh ladies and gentlemen over there... I should've left that place long ago!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heh... Mr. Brightside here...

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: Sure, that's me! Yesterday is yesterday, today is today, and tomorrow is always a new day.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: All bad things should be treated just like fish — thrown out when the day is done. That's the secret to keeping life fresh.

dialogues.speaker: Lawaia
dialogues.text: (Lawaia gives you a playful wink.)
